theme: Vrbo / HomeAway datasets and scrapers, Vrbo listing snapshots, Expedia Group vacation rental supply data
queries_run: gh search repos "vacation rental dataset" --limit 30 --sort stars
gh search repos "expedia group" data --limit 30 --sort stars

candidates.name: hospitality-python
candidates.what_it_holds: Municipal (Chapel Hill, NC) internal repo with two scripts: extract-airbnb-properties.py (uses the unofficial nderkach/airbnb-python API client) and extract-vrbo-properties.py (basic screen-scraping of Vrbo listing pages), aggregating output into a single CSV of short-term rental listings with lat/long for the town. Marked 'internal use only - experimental'; authors note data quality is low and manual cleanup is required.
candidates.why_useful: One of very few public repos that actually attempts a Vrbo listing pull (gap #9, competitor/adjacent supply). Method only, not usable as-is (low quality, unofficial API, would need running against live sites which is a ToS question), but demonstrates the closest thing to a Vrbo scraper with a real, if small, municipal use case (Chapel Hill).
candidates.time_coverage: unknown / one-off pull, no dated vintages
candidates.size_hint: small municipal CSV, unspecified row count

candidates.name: booking-sites-parser
candidates.what_it_holds: PHP CLI parser targeting Booking.com, Homeaway.com and Airbnb.com listing pages; invoked as a module or CLI with a listing URL argument. README does not document exact fields extracted; no committed data files, no evidence of active maintenance or a version tag.
candidates.why_useful: A generic multi-site (incl. Homeaway) listing parser could in principle be pointed at Vrbo/Expedia vacation-rental pages to pull price/amenity fields, addressing gap #9, but it is unmaintained tooling with no data attached and unclear scope; scraping would also be a ToS decision.

candidates.name: vrbo-calendar-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Small script that scrapes a single Vrbo property's public calendar page and returns a list of available/booked dates for that listing.
candidates.why_useful: Method for pulling Vrbo per-listing calendar availability, which is the raw ingredient behind occupancy/booking-lead-time metrics (gap #2/#3) analogous to Inside Airbnb calendar dumps, but scoped to one listing at a time with no aggregation or committed panel.

candidates.name: web-crawler-with-proxies
candidates.what_it_holds: A web crawler specifically for Vrbo.com using Crawlera API and Hotspot Shield VPN as proxy layers to evade anti-bot defenses; crawler code only, no committed dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms feasibility (and the anti-bot difficulty) of building a Vrbo listing crawler; would need real infrastructure and is explicitly a ToS decision to run — catalogued as a method, not usable off the shelf.

candidates.name: vrbo-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Vacation-rental scraper for Vrbo covering property discovery, detail extraction, pricing, amenities and geolocation, with anti-bot handling built in. No committed dataset in the repo; framework/tooling only.
candidates.why_useful: The most feature-complete open Vrbo scraper found (pricing + amenities + geolocation fields, not just calendar dates), so if a human later authorizes scraping it is the best-documented starting method for gap #9/#2; currently zero stars and no data delivered.

candidates.name: vrbo-extractor-4-0
candidates.what_it_holds: Described as a 'comprehensive VRBO listings and reviews scraper'; no data files visible in the search result, code/tooling repo only, very recent and unstarred.
candidates.why_useful: Another candidate Vrbo scraping method (listings + reviews) for gap #9 if scraping is later authorized; unverified maturity.

candidates.name: vrbo_prices
candidates.what_it_holds: Tool to pull Vrbo listings and their relative rental prices; small personal repo, no evidence of a committed dataset from the search metadata alone.
candidates.why_useful: Another Vrbo price-pulling method touching gap #2 (realised/asked pricing for STRs) if usable; needs inspection to confirm any data files are actually committed.

candidates.name: homeaway_api_ruby
candidates.what_it_holds: Official (now-archived, org name still 'homeaway') Ruby SDK for the HomeAway Partner/API — auth and endpoint wrappers for listings/reservations, not a dataset. The underlying HomeAway public API is defunct post Vrbo/Expedia consolidation, so the client likely no longer resolves against a live endpoint.
candidates.why_useful: Historical evidence of what an official HomeAway API surface looked like (listing/reservation objects); of essentially no practical pull value today since HomeAway's own API has been retired, but documents the data schema HomeAway once exposed.

candidates.name: bnbCalendar
candidates.what_it_holds: Small tool that syncs Airbnb and Vrbo iCal calendar feeds together for a host managing both platforms (team scheduling use case), not a dataset or scraper of public listings.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms iCal feeds are the standard cross-platform availability format hosts use between Airbnb and Vrbo; marginal — it is a host-side ops tool, not a data source, but shows the iCal route into per-listing occupancy exists for both platforms.

candidates.name: vrbo-listings-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Repo named as a Vrbo listings API wrapper/client; no description or stars, contents unverified beyond the name from search metadata.
candidates.why_useful: Possible additional Vrbo access method; flagged for completeness but unverified — needs a README check before relying on it.

candidates.name: SIGNAL-STR-Listing-Matcher
candidates.what_it_holds: A Flask app that resolves a physical address + unit number to its live Airbnb/Vrbo listing, tested across three commercial STR data platforms (Apify, AirROI, RapidAPI) using a direct-lookup-first, geocode-and-filter-fallback strategy. No data committed; it is a matcher/orchestrator that calls paid third-party STR data APIs (Apify, AirROI, RapidAPI), not a free data source itself.
candidates.why_useful: Useful map of which commercial vendors (AirROI, Apify STR scrapers, RapidAPI STR listing endpoints) exist for address-to-listing matching across Airbnb+Vrbo — worth knowing as a paid-vendor landscape reference even though it delivers no free data itself and would require paid keys we are told not to use.

candidates.name: ExpediaGroup GitHub org (general)
candidates.what_it_holds: Expedia Group's official GitHub org publishes engineering OSS (e.g. the deprecated service-client-statsd plugin found in search) but, from this search, no vacation-rental supply/listing/ADR datasets — Expedia's public repos are infra/tooling (GraphQL federation, streaming libs, service clients), not travel-metric data exports.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms Expedia Group does not appear to publish open vacation-rental supply or booking-volume data on GitHub; worth noting as a negative result so future scouts don't re-check the org expecting a data dump.

notes: This theme is unusually barren on GitHub: 'vrbo' and 'homeaway' as bare search terms are dominated by (a) unrelated VR/robotics repos that happen to match the 'VR' substring, and (b) dozens of student full-stack-bootcamp 'Airbnb clone' / 'Vrbo clone' web apps (Next.js/MERN/Rails) that use the Vrbo name only as a UI theme and contain zero real listing data or scraping logic — all excluded per instructions. No repo found holds a committed Vrbo/HomeAway dataset (CSV/parquet of listings, prices, or calendars) of any real size; everything real is scraper/client CODE with no data attached, and HomeAway's own public API appears defunct since the Vrbo/Expedia consolidation. No Kaggle-style vacation-rental-dataset repo (i.e. nothing like Inside Airbnb but for Vrbo) exists publicly on GitHub as far as 6 gh search calls could surface. Recommend to the orchestrator: if this gap (#9, Vrbo/HomeAway supply) needs to be filled, the realistic paths are (1) a human-authorized scraping project built on one of the scraper repos above (Edioff/vrbo-scraper looks most complete), or (2) a paid vendor (AirROI, Apify STR store, Key Data, AirDNA) rather than free/open data — none of which are gh-cataloguable as 'data already there'. Did not exceed the 6 gh-search-call budget; used 2 WebFetch README pulls instead of gh api to stay within limits.
